title: Introduce SLO drift detector and backpressure harmonizer
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds an SLO drift detector that triggers coordinated, non-disruptive backpressure across regions. Default mode is opt-in; rollout started as canary. Includes telemetry + runbook links.
description:
Context: We observed transient SLO divergence in certain regional clusters when KV pressure + bursty longest-seq requests coincided. Existing circuit state updates were too coarse to avoid cascades: nodes would flip to hard-circuit and downstream regions experienced sudden failover spikes. This PR introduces two complementary components: (1) an SLO Drift Detector that watches per-tenant/per-route latency & error slopes against baseline windows and emits a graded alert (drift_score), and (2) a Backpressure Harmonizer that consumes drift_score to apply temporary, coordinated soft-shedding adjustments and paced KV-drain directives across affected regions.

Motivation: Reduce cascading hard failovers by (a) detecting slow, progressive SLO degradation earlier, (b) applying smoother, temporally-scoped backpressure rather than binary circuit flips, and (c) ensuring KV cache drains and slot reservations are harmonized so rejoin/reopen oscillations are minimized. This is intended as a stability-first mechanism that can operate during autoscaler events, hardware maintenance, and noisy neighbor spikes.

What changed (high-level commits):
- commit 1: add slo/detector service with sliding-window drift scoring + config (monitored metrics: p50/p90/p99 latency, error_rate, token_throttle_rate)
- commit 2: harmonizer control plane + operators (region coordinator, soft-shed recipes, KV-drain pacing)
- commit 3: API surface + runtime hooks (runtime: check drift_score before admission decision; introduce admission override backoff)
- commit 4: telemetry: new metrics, tag enrichment, and rollout events schema
- commit 5: unit + integration tests for drift detection thresholds and harmonizer pacing
- commit 6: docs: runbook + console UI additions for on-call visibility
- commit 7: migration: db schema for drift records + feature flag gating

Files/areas changed (illustrative):
- runtime/admission/score_gate.go (new hook that reads drift_score)
- slo/detector/service.go (main scoring loop + anomaly smoothing)
- controlplane/harmonizer/region_coordinator.go (synchronizes soft-shed directives)
- telemetry/metrics_definitions.yaml (+ new tags: drift_score, harmonizer_tier)
- migrations/20260212_add_drift_records.sql
- docs/runbooks/slo-drift-and-harmonizer.md
- web/console/src/routes/slo-harmonizer.tsx (small UI for manual nudge & visibility)
- tests/integration/harmonizer_e2e_test.go

Small config example applied by the PR (default canary values):
{ "slo_detector": {"window_seconds": 300, "min_samples": 50, "drift_threshold": 0.12}, "harmonizer": {"max_soft_shed": 0.15, "kv_drain_rate_per_min": 0.02, "hold_seconds": 180} }

Review summary / discussion highlights: 
- Arman Patel (approver): Requested that drift_score be versioned and backwards-compatible in the schema to avoid downstream mismatches; asked for an integration test simulating staggered regional failures. Response: added schema versioning header (+1 commit) and included an integration scenario that runs a 3-region staggered spike.
- Sofia Ruiz (SRE): Raised concern about metric cardinality from per-tenant drift tagging. Requested sampling fallback and a cold-path aggregator. Response: implemented tiered sampling (per-tenant only for enterprise plans, aggregated buckets for free/low-tier) and added aggregator in telemetry (commit 4).
- Lars Bergstrom (runtime): Asked for a safe default that is effectively off for Dedicated customers unless explicitly opted-in. Response: feature-flag gating and Dedicated-preset set to opt-out by default; can be switched via admin flags in private installs.
- Review thread included one requested change to reduce default max_soft_shed from 20% to 15% to avoid client-visible degradation; author accepted and adjusted.

CI / testing notes: Initial CI run had a flaky e2e failure for harmonizer timing (test timeout). I reproduced locally and increased test timeouts + added a deterministic clock in tests; reran CI and all checks passed. CI summary: unit tests (pass), integration e2e (pass after rerun), lint (pass), perf-bench (smoke, pass), security-scan (pass, no new findings).

Deployment / rollout plan: Canary on main hosted region (1% traffic) for 24h, monitor drift_score and harmonizer metrics (slo_drift_incidents, harmonizer_applied_ratio). If stable, increment to 10% -> 25% -> 100% over the week with rollback capability via console toggle. For Dedicated/private customers the feature is gated; we included operator instructions in docs/runbooks/slo-drift-and-harmonizer.md.

Operational runbook highlights:
- If harmonizer_applied_ratio is high and SLOs don't recover in 5 minutes, disable harmonizer and switch to documented fallback (manual throttle + canary node removal).
- Use console "nudge" UI to temporarily lower max_soft_shed in a region.
- Investigate KV pressure metrics if KV-drain directives are frequent; consider increasing kv_drain_rate_per_min or scaling cache nodes.

Post-merge actions: 
- Create monitoring alert ENG-4128 to auto-open Linear when drift_score > 0.25 for 3 windows in a row for a production region.
- Schedule a follow-up to add heuristic for model-size-aware drift baselines (ENG-4206).

Merge outcome: Squash-and-merge on 2026-02-18 after approvals from Arman and Sofia. Merge commit includes a concise changelog and a migration runner that is safe to run in rolling fashion.

Notes and rationale for reviewers: Focused on non-disruptive, incremental controls; avoided adding hard-circuit triggers; aim is to reduce incident blast radius by smoothing decisions at the control plane rather than changing underlying admission semantics. This PR is intentionally conservative in default values to minimize customer-visible impact.

If anything regresses after rollout please ping SRE on-call and tag ENG-4128/SRE-87 in the incident. Runbook and console docs included in the PR provide the commands for immediate disable and KV-drain cancellation.
